title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 13
paragraphs: Perceiving what the Ionians were doing, the commanders of the Samians then at length accepted from Aeaces son of Syloson the proposals that Aeaces had earlier sent at the Persians' bidding, asking them to leave the Ionian alliance. The Samians, I say, accepted these proposals, seeing that there was great lack of discipline on the Ionians' part, while at the same time it was clear to them that it was impossible to overcome the king's power; and they knew well also that even if they should overcome Darius's present naval force, another would be upon them five times as large. Having found a pretext, then, as soon as they saw that the Ionians refused to be of service, they counted it gain for themselves to save their temples and their private property. Now Aeaces, from whom the Samians accepted the proposals, was the son of Syloson, the son of Aeaces; and being tyrant of Samos, he had been deprived of his rule by Aristagoras the Milesian, like the other tyrants of Ionia.
